pointers.sentence: The built-in tags of `django.template.defaulttags` are in every Django template without `{% load %}`: how `{% for %}` builds its loop variables, `{% if %}` parses a condition with `django/template/smartif.py` and `{% url %}` reverses a name, and how `{% cycle %}`, `{% ifchanged %}`, `{% regroup %}` and `{% querystring %}` work.
The module is one of the three libraries every `Engine` gives each parser before the first token (`django/template/engine.py:Engine.__init__`).
Each tag in it but two is written there as a compile function and a subclass of `Node` (`django/template/base.py:Node`).

`do_for` reads `{% for ship in ships %}` at compile time: at least four words, an optional last word `reversed`, loop variables split on commas, the sequence as a filter expression, the body up to `{% empty %}` or `{% endfor %}` (`django/template/defaulttags.py:do_for`).
`ForNode.render` then works in this order (`django/template/defaulttags.py:ForNode.render`):
`{{ forloop.length }}` is new (`docs/releases/6.0.txt`).

`do_if` parses the condition of `{% if %}` and of each `{% elif %}`, and each branch up to the next clause, into an `IfNode` of pairs, a condition and a node list; `{% else %}` has `None` for its condition (`django/template/defaulttags.py:do_if`).
The condition is parsed by `django/template/smartif.py`, a top-down operator-precedence parser.

`OPERATORS` holds a class for each operator, made by `infix` or `prefix` from a power and a function: `"or"` at 6, `"and"` at 7, the prefix `"not"` at 8, `"in"` and `"not in"` at 9, and `"is"`, `"is not"` and the six comparisons at 10 (`django/template/smartif.py:infix`).

`IfParser.__init__` joins `is` `not` and `not` `in` into single tokens and makes each word a fresh operator or, failing that, an operand, which `TemplateIfParser` makes a `TemplateLiteral` around a compiled filter expression, so `ships|length` is one operand (`django/template/defaulttags.py:TemplateIfParser`).
An operator's `led` parses its right side with its own power, so equal powers group to the left (`django/template/smartif.py:IfParser.expression`).
`IfNode.render` renders the first branch whose condition holds (`django/template/defaulttags.py:IfNode.render`).

An operator evaluates its operands in its function, so `and` and `or` stop early, and turns any exception into `False`; a comment in `infix` says a template should not raise while rendering (`django/template/smartif.py:infix`).

`{% url %}` compiles its first argument, the name, as a filter expression, so it may be quoted or a variable; takes `as` and a name off the end; and makes each other word a keyword argument, `pk=port.pk`, or a positional one, by `kwarg_re` (`django/template/defaulttags.py:url`).

`URLNode.render` resolves them and calls `reverse` ([Reversing a name](../urls/reversing.md)) with a current application from the context's request: its attribute `"current_app"`, else the namespace of `HttpRequest.resolver_match` ([Namespaces](../urls/namespaces.md#where-the-current-application-comes-from)) (`django/template/defaulttags.py:URLNode.render`).

`{% with total=port.ships|length %}` pushes a level holding its names until `{% endwith %}`; `do_with` reads the pairs, or the older `port.ships|length as total`, with `token_kwargs` (`django/template/base.py:token_kwargs`).

Every value is resolved before the push, so `{% with a=1 b=a %}` gives b the a from outside, and a missing variable in one becomes `"string_if_invalid"` (`django/template/defaulttags.py:WithNode.render`).

Given `as` and a name, `{% url %}`, `{% firstof %}`, `{% now %}`, `{% widthratio %}` and the simple tags assign it in the context's top level, as `{% regroup %}` does (`django/template/context.py:BaseContext.__setitem__`): set inside `{% for %}`, `{% with %}` or `{% block %}`, it is gone after the end tag, and inside `{% if %}`, which pushes nothing, it outlasts it.
`CycleNode` keeps its place in the render context under the node itself: an iterator cycling through its compiled values, made at its first render (`django/template/defaulttags.py:CycleNode.render`).

`Template.render` gives the render context a fresh level, and `{% include %}` renders its template that way each time ([Rendering: nodes and the render context](rendering.md)), so `{% cycle 'odd' 'even' %}` in a template included once for each of three ships renders `"odd"` all three times (`django/template/base.py:Template.render`).
Named nodes are kept on the parser, so a name holds within one template; `{% cycle row %}` returns the same node, and every use advances it (`django/template/defaulttags.py:cycle`).
`{% resetcycle %}` gives a fresh iterator to the named node or, with no name, to the last cycle tag before it that declared values (`django/template/defaulttags.py:resetcycle`).

`IfChangedNode` renders its body when its arguments' values, or with none its rendered body, differ from last time, and otherwise its `{% else %}` branch or nothing (`django/template/defaulttags.py:IfChangedNode.render`).

It keeps the last values under the node in the loop's `"forloop"` dictionary, which is new each time the loop starts, so in a nested loop the comparison starts over on each pass of the outer one; outside a loop, in the render context (`django/template/defaulttags.py:IfChangedNode._get_context_stack_frame`).

The key is compiled as the variable `{{ kinds.kind }}`, and each ship is put in the context under kinds while its key resolves: a hack, its comment says, for want of a getattr that works through the context (`django/template/defaulttags.py:regroup`).
Each is a `GroupedResult` of `"grouper"` and `"list"`; a missing list gives no groups (`django/template/defaulttags.py:RegroupNode.render`).
`querystring` is a simple tag that takes the context (`django/template/defaulttags.py:querystring`).
The `"?"` is always there, and several positional mappings are allowed (`docs/releases/6.0.txt`).
| `{% firstof %}` | the first true argument, escaped when autoescaping is on | `django/template/defaulttags.py:FirstOfNode` |
| `{% now %}` | the time now, through the date filter; its argument is not resolved, only stripped of its first and last characters | `django/template/defaulttags.py:now` |
| `{% spaceless %}` | the body with white space between tags, and at its ends, removed | `django/template/defaulttags.py:SpacelessNode` |
| `{% verbatim %}` | the body as text, which the lexer left unparsed | `django/template/defaulttags.py:verbatim` |
| `{% templatetag %}` | a delimiter of the syntax, by name | `django/template/defaulttags.py:TemplateTagNode` |
| `{% widthratio %}` | a value over a maximum, times a width, rounded half to even | `django/template/defaulttags.py:WidthRatioNode` |
| `{% filter %}` | the body through filters, refusing the escape and safe filters | `django/template/defaulttags.py:do_filter` |
| `{% lorem %}` | placeholder Latin | `django/template/defaulttags.py:LoremNode` |
| `{% debug %}` | the context and the loaded modules, when `settings.DEBUG` is true ([Template errors and debug information](debugging.md)) | `django/template/defaulttags.py:DebugNode` |
| `{% comment %}` | nothing: the parser skips to `{% endcomment %}` unparsed | `django/template/defaulttags.py:comment` |
| `{% csrf_token %}` | a hidden input holding the CSRF context processor's token, or nothing when the context has none | `django/template/defaulttags.py:CsrfTokenNode` |

| `{% csp_nonce_attr %}` | a simple tag: `nonce="…"` from the nonce of `django.template.context_processors.csp`, or nothing; given a form's media, its tags, with that nonce on all but those given as ready HTML | `django/utils/csp.py:nonce_attr` |
